sections.content: Colorado Springs has quietly become one of the most compelling real estate markets in the Mountain West. Sitting at the base of Pikes Peak with a population of over 480,000, it offers something Denver stopped offering years ago: affordability. For investors hunting real estate deals in Colorado Springs CO, the combination of military-driven rental demand, steady population growth, and a lower price-per-door than the state capital makes this city worth serious attention. Whether you are just getting started or expanding a portfolio, this guide covers everything you need to know — from average home prices to the best neighborhoods and deal types available right now. If you are brand new to the game, bookmark our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide first, then come back here ready to go deep on this specific market.
Colorado Springs Market Overview: What the Numbers Say

As of mid-2024, the median home price in Colorado Springs sits around $430,000 — roughly $200,000 below Denver's median. That gap is significant for investors calculating margins on flips or cash flow on rentals. The market has cooled slightly from its 2021-2022 peak frenzy, which is actually good news: motivated sellers are more common, days on market have stretched from under two weeks to 30-45 days in many zip codes, and the bidding war insanity has largely faded. Inventory remains tight relative to demand, but not so tight that you cannot negotiate. The city added roughly 15,000 new residents between 2020 and 2023, and that pace shows no signs of reversing. Military relocation alone — driven by Fort Carson, Peterson Space Force Base, and the Air Force Academy — keeps rental vacancy rates consistently below 5%, a number that makes landlords smile.
Key Market Stats at a Glance

items: Average days on market: 30–45 days (up from 10-12 in 2022)
Year-over-year price appreciation: roughly 3–4% (stabilized after 20%+ pandemic spike)
Major employment anchors: military installations, aerospace, healthcare, tourism

sections.content: Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Deals in Colorado Springs CO

Not every zip code in Colorado Springs performs the same way for investors. The north side of the city — particularly areas like Briargate, Northgate, and Flying Horse — tends to attract higher-income buyers and features newer construction. These neighborhoods are great for appreciation plays but tight on cash flow. For investors focused on margins, the better opportunities tend to cluster in specific pockets worth knowing well.
Neighborhoods Worth Watching

items: Fountain Valley / Security-Widefield: South of Fort Carson, this area has lower price points ($280,000–$360,000), high military renter concentration, and steady turnover that creates wholesaling and rental opportunities regularly.

East Colorado Springs (80909, 80910): One of the best value-add markets in the city. Older housing stock, motivated sellers, and prices that still allow for $50,000–$80,000 flip margins when the rehab is managed tightly.

Pueblo West (just south): Technically outside city limits but within the metro investment zone — land is cheap, and buy-and-hold investors are finding strong cap rates on new builds and value-add duplexes.
Downtown / Old Colorado City: Higher price tags, but short-term rental demand is strong due to tourism. Zoning research is essential here before committing.
Cimarron Hills: An unincorporated community east of the city with affordable SFR stock and a renter-heavy demographic — solid for long-term hold strategies.

Types of Deals Available: Wholesale, Flip, or Rental?
Wholesaling in Colorado Springs

Wholesaling is alive and well here. The east side and Fountain Valley area generate a steady stream of distressed properties — probate sales, pre-foreclosures, tired landlords, and inherited homes that need work. Assignment fees in the $10,000–$25,000 range are realistic on deals where the ARV is $300,000–$400,000 and the seller accepts a price that leaves room for a rehabber's margin. If you are new to this strategy, start with our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide to understand the mechanics before you start making offers. Colorado does not require a real estate license to wholesale, but you need to structure contracts correctly and stay within legal guidelines on assignment language.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

Flippers who know their numbers are doing well in Colorado Springs. The east side offers the best entry prices — homes in the $200,000–$280,000 range that can retail at $360,000–$420,000 after a clean, well-scoped renovation. The key is staying disciplined on rehab budgets. Labor costs in Colorado Springs are lower than Denver but have climbed 20–30% since 2020. A full gut renovation on a 1,400-square-foot home might run $80,000–$110,000 depending on finish level. Target light-to-medium cosmetic flips in the $30,000–$55,000 rehab range for the fastest velocity and the lowest execution risk. Use the [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to back into your maximum allowable offer before you ever sit down with a seller.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

The military relocation pipeline makes Colorado Springs one of the most landlord-friendly rental markets in the state. Fort Carson alone processes thousands of PCS (Permanent Change of Station) moves per year, and those service members need quality, well-located housing fast. A 3-bedroom, 2-bath home in Security-Widefield renting for $1,900/month against an all-in purchase price of $300,000 produces a gross rent multiplier under 160 and a potential cap rate in the 5–6% range — competitive for a Colorado market. Add in the appreciation upside and the low vacancy risk, and the long-term hold case is strong.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Colorado Springs

The best real estate deals in Colorado Springs CO are rarely listed on the MLS. Savvy investors are finding them through direct mail campaigns targeting probate and tax-delinquent lists, driving for dollars in older neighborhoods, building relationships with local wholesalers, and leveraging data tools to identify distressed properties before they hit the market. Our detailed breakdown of [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) covers the full playbook, but the short version for Colorado Springs is this: focus your skip-tracing and outreach on properties in zip codes 80909, 80910, and 80911, where you will find the highest concentration of tired landlords and aging ownership with equity. County courthouse records, the El Paso County Assessor's website, and probate filings are all publicly accessible starting points.

"The best deals are never found — they're built. You build them through relationships, consistency, and the ability to move fast when a motivated seller appears." — Common wisdom among experienced wholesalers and investors in competitive regional markets.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Eyeing Colorado Springs

Investing remotely in Colorado Springs is absolutely doable — many successful landlords and flippers operate from out of state — but it requires building the right local team before you commit capital. Here is a practical checklist to get started the right way.

items: Build your boots-on-the-ground team first: Find a local investor-friendly real estate agent, a reliable property manager (especially important for military tenant turnover), and a general contractor with references you can verify.

Understand Colorado landlord-tenant law: Colorado has specific notice requirements, security deposit rules, and habitability standards. Non-compliance is expensive. Consult a local real estate attorney before signing your first lease.
Visit before you buy: Even one 3-day trip to walk neighborhoods, meet your PM, and inspect the property in person will save you from remote-buying mistakes that are very hard to undo.

Use data to underwrite remotely: Platforms like AIWholesail's [Colorado Springs market dashboard](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/colorado-springs-co) give you comparable sales, rental rate benchmarks, and neighborhood-level performance data so you can analyze deals from anywhere before booking a flight.

Account for Colorado's hail risk: El Paso County is in a high-hail-frequency zone. Factor in insurance costs and potential roof replacement into every acquisition analysis — surprises here have stung many out-of-state buyers.

Learn to [analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals): Remote investing has zero margin for sloppy underwriting. Master your numbers before you make your first offer.

sections.content: Local Market Trends Shaping Investor Strategy in 2024

Several trends are worth watching as you build your Colorado Springs strategy. First, interest rates above 7% have pushed a segment of would-be buyers back into the rental pool, which is a tailwind for landlords. Second, the Space Force and aerospace sector expansion around Peterson AFB is attracting higher-income tenants and buyers to the northeast quadrant of the city — a longer-term appreciation play. Third, the city has been proactive about new development permitting in areas like Banning Lewis Ranch on the far east side, which will add housing supply but also signals long-term confidence in demand. Finally, short-term rental regulations have tightened in some parts of the city, so if you are considering Airbnb or VRBO, verify current zoning and licensing rules for your specific address before counting on that income stream.
